meta.name: mathkix_prerequisite_map
meta.description: Prerequisite map for Common Core Math Standards, Grades 3 through High School. Each node represents a standard with its prerequisites. The algorithm should traverse this graph to find the deepest unmastered prerequisite for any target skill.
notes: Prerequisites prefixed with 'K.', '1.', or '2.' are foundational entry points assumed mastered by Grade 3.
Standards marked with (+) are advanced/optional for college-readiness.

3.OA.1.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division
3.OA.1.description: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each.

3.OA.2.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division
3.OA.2.description: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share.

3.OA.3.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division
3.OA.3.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities.

3.OA.4.cluster: Represent and solve problems involving multiplication and division
3.OA.4.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers.

3.OA.5.cluster: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division
3.OA.5.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide (commutative, associative, distributive).

3.OA.6.cluster: Understand properties of multiplication and the relationship between multiplication and division
3.OA.6.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem.

3.OA.7.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100. By end of Grade 3, know from memory all products of two one-digit numbers.

3.OA.8.cluster: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic
3.OA.8.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations. Represent with equations using a letter for the unknown.

3.OA.9.cluster: Solve problems involving the four operations, and identify and explain patterns in arithmetic
3.OA.9.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including in addition/multiplication tables) and explain them using properties of operations.

3.NBT.1.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
3.NBT.1.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
3.NBT.1.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

3.NBT.2.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
3.NBT.2.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
3.NBT.2.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

3.NBT.3.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
3.NBT.3.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
3.NBT.3.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90.

3.NF.1.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.1.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b.

3.NF.2.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.2.description: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line; represent fractions on a number line diagram.

3.NF.2a.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.2a.description: Represent a fraction 1/b on a number line by partitioning the interval from 0 to 1 into b equal parts.

3.NF.2b.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.2b.description: Represent a fraction a/b on a number line by marking off a lengths 1/b from 0.

3.NF.3.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.3.description: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases, and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

3.NF.3a.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.3a.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are the same size or same point on a number line.

3.NF.3b.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.3b.description: Recognize and generate simple equivalent fractions, e.g., 1/2 = 2/4, 4/6 = 2/3.

3.NF.3c.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.3c.description: Express whole numbers as fractions and recognize fractions equivalent to whole numbers.

3.NF.3d.cluster: Develop understanding of fractions as numbers
3.NF.3d.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or same denominator by reasoning about their size.

3.MD.1.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects
3.MD.1.description: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals in minutes. Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals.

3.MD.2.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and estimation of intervals of time, liquid volumes, and masses of objects
3.MD.2.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using grams, kilograms, and liters.

3.MD.3.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set. Solve 'how many more/less' problems using bar graphs.

3.MD.4.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths using rulers marked with halves and fourths of an inch. Show data on a line plot.

3.MD.5.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition
3.MD.5.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures and understand concepts of area measurement (unit squares).

3.MD.5a.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area
3.MD.5a.description: A unit square has one square unit of area and can be used to measure area.

3.MD.5b.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area
3.MD.5b.description: A plane figure covered by n unit squares without gaps or overlaps has an area of n square units.

3.MD.6.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition
3.MD.6.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares.

3.MD.7.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of area and relate area to multiplication and to addition
3.MD.7.description: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

3.MD.7a.description: Find area of a rectangle by tiling and show area equals side lengths multiplied.

3.MD.7b.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles in real-world and math problems.

3.MD.7c.description: Use tiling to show area of a rectangle with sides a and b+c is the sum of a×b and a×c (distributive property via area).

3.MD.7d.description: Recognize area as additive. Find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing into non-overlapping rectangles.

3.MD.8.cluster: Geometric measurement: recognize perimeter as an attribute of plane figures
3.MD.8.description: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding perimeter, unknown side lengths, and comparing rectangles with same perimeter/different areas.

3.G.1.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes
3.G.1.description: Understand shapes in different categories may share attributes defining a larger category (e.g., quadrilaterals). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, squares as quadrilaterals.

3.G.2.cluster: Reason with shapes and their attributes
3.G.2.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole.

4.OA.1.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems
4.OA.1.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g., 35 = 5 × 7 means 35 is 5 times as many as 7).

4.OA.2.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems
4.OA.2.description: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison.

4.OA.3.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems
4.OA.3.description: Solve multistep word problems with whole numbers using the four operations, including interpreting remainders.

4.OA.4.cluster: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples
4.OA.4.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number 1–100. Determine if a number is a multiple of a given one-digit number. Determine prime or composite.

4.OA.5.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule. Identify features of the pattern not explicit in the rule.

4.NBT.1.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.1.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers
4.NBT.1.description: Recognize that a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

4.NBT.2.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.2.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers
4.NBT.2.description: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare using >, =, <.

4.NBT.3.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.3.cluster: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers
4.NBT.3.description: Use place value understanding to round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.

4.NBT.4.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.4.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
4.NBT.4.description: Fluently add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

4.NBT.5.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.5.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
4.NBT.5.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number, and multiply two two-digit numbers.

4.NBT.6.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
4.NBT.6.cluster: Use place value understanding and properties of operations to perform multi-digit arithmetic
4.NBT.6.description: Find whole-number quotients and remainders with up to four-digit dividends and one-digit divisors.

4.NF.1.cluster: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering
4.NF.1.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to (n×a)/(n×b) using visual fraction models.

4.NF.2.cluster: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering
4.NF.2.description: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators by creating common denominators/numerators or comparing to 1/2.

4.NF.3.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

4.NF.3a.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.

4.NF.3b.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way.

4.NF.3c.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.

4.NF.3d.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators.

4.NF.4.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

4.NF.4a.description: Understand a fraction a/b as a multiple of 1/b (e.g., 5/4 = 5 × (1/4)).

4.NF.4b.description: Understand a multiple of a/b as a multiple of 1/b, and use this to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

4.NF.4c.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.

4.NF.5.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions
4.NF.5.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100; add fractions with denominators 10 and 100.

4.NF.6.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions
4.NF.6.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100.

4.NF.7.cluster: Understand decimal notation for fractions, and compare decimal fractions
4.NF.7.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths by reasoning about their size.

4.MD.1.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements
4.MD.1.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system. Express measurements in a larger unit in terms of a smaller unit.

4.MD.2.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements
4.MD.2.description: Use the four operations to solve word problems involving distances, time, volumes, masses, and money including simple fractions/decimals.

4.MD.3.cluster: Solve problems involving measurement and conversion of measurements
4.MD.3.description: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real world and mathematical problems.

4.MD.4.description: Make a line plot for measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems using line plots.

4.MD.5.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles
4.MD.5.description: Recognize angles as geometric shapes formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint. Understand angle measurement concepts.

4.MD.5a.description: An angle is measured by the fraction of the circular arc between the two rays. One degree = 1/360 of a circle.

4.MD.5b.description: An angle that turns through n one-degree angles has an angle measure of n degrees.

4.MD.6.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles
4.MD.6.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor. Sketch angles of specified measure.

4.MD.7.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of angle and measure angles
4.MD.7.description: Recognize angle measure as additive. Solve addition/subtraction problems to find unknown angles.

4.G.1.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes
4.G.1.description: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles (right, acute, obtuse), and perpendicular and parallel lines. Identify in 2D figures.

4.G.2.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes
4.G.2.description: Classify 2D figures based on presence/absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or angles of a specified size. Recognize right triangles.

4.G.3.cluster: Draw and identify lines and angles, and classify shapes
4.G.3.description: Recognize a line of symmetry for a 2D figure. Identify line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry.

5.OA.1.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions, and evaluate expressions with these symbols.

5.OA.2.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them.

5.OA.3.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules. Identify relationships between corresponding terms. Graph ordered pairs on a coordinate plane.

5.NBT.1.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.1.description: Recognize that a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as the place to its right and 1/10 of the place to its left.

5.NBT.2.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.2.description: Explain patterns in the number of zeros when multiplying by powers of 10. Explain patterns in decimal point placement. Use whole-number exponents for powers of 10.

5.NBT.3.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.3.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

5.NBT.3a.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.3a.description: Read and write decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.

5.NBT.3b.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.3b.description: Compare two decimals to thousandths using >, =, <.

5.NBT.4.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.4.description: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

5.NBT.5.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.5.cluster: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths
5.NBT.5.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers using the standard algorithm.

5.NBT.6.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.6.cluster: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths
5.NBT.6.description: Find whole-number quotients with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors.

5.NBT.7.domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
5.NBT.7.cluster: Perform operations with multi-digit whole numbers and with decimals to hundredths
5.NBT.7.description: Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals to hundredths.

5.NF.1.cluster: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions
5.NF.1.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing with equivalent fractions.

5.NF.2.cluster: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions
5.NF.2.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators.

5.NF.3.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions
5.NF.3.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b).

5.NF.4.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions
5.NF.4.description: Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

5.NF.4a.description: Interpret (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts.

5.NF.4b.description: Find area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling. Multiply fractional side lengths to find areas.

5.NF.5.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions

5.NF.5a.description: Compare the size of a product to one factor based on the size of the other factor, without computing.

5.NF.5b.description: Explain why multiplying by a fraction > 1 gives a larger product and < 1 gives a smaller product.

5.NF.6.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions
5.NF.6.description: Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers.

5.NF.7.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide fractions
5.NF.7.description: Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

5.NF.7a.description: Interpret division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number and compute such quotients.

5.NF.7b.description: Interpret division of a whole number by a unit fraction and compute such quotients.

5.NF.7c.description: Solve real world problems involving division of unit fractions by whole numbers and vice versa.

5.MD.1.cluster: Convert like measurement units within a given measurement system
5.MD.1.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given measurement system.

5.MD.2.description: Make a line plot for measurements in fractions of a unit. Use fraction operations to solve problems from line plots.

5.MD.3.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition
5.MD.3.description: Recognize volume as an attribute of solid figures and understand concepts of volume measurement.

5.MD.3a.description: A unit cube has one cubic unit of volume and can be used to measure volume.

5.MD.3b.description: A solid figure packed with n unit cubes without gaps/overlaps has a volume of n cubic units.

5.MD.4.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition
5.MD.4.description: Measure volumes by counting unit cubes.

5.MD.5.cluster: Geometric measurement: understand concepts of volume and relate volume to multiplication and to addition
5.MD.5.description: Relate volume to multiplication and addition and solve real world problems involving volume.

5.MD.5a.description: Find volume of a right rectangular prism by packing with unit cubes; show volume = edge lengths multiplied.

5.MD.5b.description: Apply formulas V = l × w × h and V = b × h for rectangular prisms.

5.MD.5c.description: Recognize volume as additive. Find volumes of composite figures by adding volumes of non-overlapping parts.

5.G.1.cluster: Graph points on the coordinate plane
5.G.1.description: Use perpendicular number lines (axes) to define a coordinate system. Locate points using ordered pairs.

5.G.2.cluster: Graph points on the coordinate plane
5.G.2.description: Represent real world problems by graphing points in the first quadrant. Interpret coordinate values in context.

5.G.3.cluster: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties
5.G.3.description: Understand that attributes of a category also belong to all subcategories (e.g., all rectangles have four right angles, squares are rectangles).

5.G.4.cluster: Classify two-dimensional figures into categories based on their properties
5.G.4.description: Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties.

6.RP.1.cluster: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems
6.RP.1.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

6.RP.2.cluster: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems
6.RP.2.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0.

6.RP.3.cluster: Understand ratio concepts and use ratio reasoning to solve problems
6.RP.3.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

6.RP.3a.description: Make tables of equivalent ratios. Find missing values. Plot pairs on coordinate plane.

6.RP.3b.description: Solve unit rate problems including unit pricing and constant speed.

6.RP.3c.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100. Solve problems finding the whole given a part and percent.

6.RP.3d.description: Use ratio reasoning to convert measurement units.

6.NS.1.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to divide fractions by fractions
6.NS.1.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions. Solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.

6.NS.2.cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
6.NS.2.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

6.NS.3.cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
6.NS.3.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm.

6.NS.4.cluster: Compute fluently with multi-digit numbers and find common factors and multiples
6.NS.4.description: Find GCF of two numbers ≤ 100 and LCM of two numbers ≤ 12. Use distributive property to express sums.

6.NS.5.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers
6.NS.5.description: Understand positive and negative numbers describe quantities with opposite directions/values.

6.NS.6.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers
6.NS.6.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line. Extend to negative number coordinates.

6.NS.6a.description: Recognize opposite signs indicate locations on opposite sides of 0. –(–3) = 3. 0 is its own opposite.

6.NS.6b.description: Understand signs in ordered pairs as indicating locations in quadrants. Reflections across axes.

6.NS.6c.description: Find and position integers and other rational numbers on number line and coordinate plane.

6.NS.7.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers
6.NS.7.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers.

6.NS.7a.description: Interpret inequality statements as statements about relative position on a number line.

6.NS.7b.description: Write, interpret, and explain statements of order for rational numbers in real-world contexts.

6.NS.7c.description: Understand absolute value as distance from 0. Interpret absolute value as magnitude in real-world.

6.NS.7d.description: Distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

6.NS.8.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of numbers to the system of rational numbers
6.NS.8.description: Solve real-world problems by graphing points in all four quadrants. Use coordinates and absolute value to find distances.

6.EE.1.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions
6.EE.1.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

6.EE.2.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions
6.EE.2.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

6.EE.2a.description: Write expressions that record operations with numbers and letters standing for numbers.

6.EE.2b.description: Identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms (sum, term, product, factor, quotient, coefficient).

6.EE.2c.description: Evaluate expressions at specific values of variables. Perform operations in conventional order.

6.EE.3.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions
6.EE.3.description: Apply properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions (e.g., distributive property).

6.EE.4.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of arithmetic to algebraic expressions
6.EE.4.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent.

6.EE.5.cluster: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities
6.EE.5.description: Understand solving an equation/inequality as finding which values make it true. Use substitution to check.

6.EE.6.cluster: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities
6.EE.6.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving problems.

6.EE.7.cluster: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities
6.EE.7.description: Solve real-world problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q.

6.EE.8.cluster: Reason about and solve one-variable equations and inequalities
6.EE.8.description: Write inequalities of the form x > c or x < c. Recognize infinitely many solutions. Represent on number line.

6.EE.9.cluster: Represent and analyze quantitative relationships between dependent and independent variables
6.EE.9.description: Use variables for two quantities that change in relationship. Write equations. Analyze with graphs and tables.

6.G.1.cluster: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume
6.G.1.description: Find area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing/decomposing.

6.G.2.cluster: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume
6.G.2.description: Find volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths. Apply V = lwh and V = bh.

6.G.3.cluster: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume
6.G.3.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates. Use coordinates to find side lengths.

6.G.4.cluster: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume
6.G.4.description: Represent 3D figures using nets of rectangles and triangles. Use nets to find surface area.

6.SP.1.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in data.

6.SP.2.description: Understand a data set has a distribution described by center, spread, and overall shape.

6.SP.3.description: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with a single number; measure of variation describes spread.

6.SP.4.description: Display numerical data in dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

6.SP.5.description: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context (number of observations, center, variability, shape).

7.RP.1.cluster: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems
7.RP.1.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas, and other quantities.

7.RP.2.cluster: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems
7.RP.2.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

7.RP.2a.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship (test equivalent ratios, graph through origin).

7.RP.2b.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions.

7.RP.2c.description: Represent proportional relationships by equations (e.g., t = pn).

7.RP.2d.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on a proportional relationship graph means, especially (0, 0) and (1, r).

7.RP.3.cluster: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems
7.RP.3.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems (interest, tax, markups, commissions, percent change, error).

7.NS.1.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to rational numbers
7.NS.1.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers.

7.NS.1a.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.

7.NS.1b.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p. Show additive inverses sum to 0.

7.NS.1c.description: Understand subtraction as adding the additive inverse. Distance between two rationals = absolute value of difference.

7.NS.1d.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

7.NS.2.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to rational numbers
7.NS.2.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division to multiply and divide rational numbers.

7.NS.2a.description: Understand multiplication extends from fractions to rational numbers maintaining properties. Rules for signed numbers.

7.NS.2b.description: Understand integers can be divided (non-zero divisor) and every quotient of integers is rational. –(p/q) = (–p)/q = p/(–q).

7.NS.2c.description: Apply properties of operations to multiply and divide rational numbers.

7.NS.2d.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know the decimal form terminates or repeats.

7.NS.3.cluster: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to rational numbers
7.NS.3.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

7.EE.1.cluster: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions
7.EE.1.description: Apply properties of operations to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

7.EE.2.cluster: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions
7.EE.2.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms can shed light on the problem.

7.EE.3.cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations
7.EE.3.description: Solve multi-step real-life problems with positive and negative rational numbers in any form. Assess reasonableness.

7.EE.4.cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations
7.EE.4.description: Use variables to represent quantities and construct simple equations and inequalities.

7.EE.4a.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r.

7.EE.4b.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r. Graph solutions.

7.G.1.cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
7.G.1.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, computing actual lengths and areas from a scale.

7.G.2.cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
7.G.2.description: Draw geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on triangle conditions (angles/sides) — unique, multiple, or none.

7.G.3.cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
7.G.3.description: Describe 2D figures that result from slicing 3D figures (plane sections of prisms and pyramids).

7.G.4.cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
7.G.4.description: Know formulas for area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.

7.G.5.cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
7.G.5.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles to write and solve equations.

7.G.6.cluster: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume
7.G.6.description: Solve problems involving area, volume, and surface area of 2D and 3D objects (triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, right prisms).

7.SP.1.cluster: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population
7.SP.1.description: Understand statistics can gain info about a population by examining a sample. Random sampling produces representative samples.

7.SP.2.cluster: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population
7.SP.2.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences. Generate multiple samples to gauge variation.

7.SP.3.cluster: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations
7.SP.3.description: Assess degree of visual overlap of two distributions. Express difference between centers as multiple of measure of variability.

7.SP.4.cluster: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations
7.SP.4.description: Use measures of center and variability from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

7.SP.5.cluster: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models
7.SP.5.description: Understand probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1.

7.SP.6.cluster: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models
7.SP.6.description: Approximate probability by collecting data (long-run relative frequency). Predict approximate relative frequency given probability.

7.SP.7.cluster: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models
7.SP.7.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities. Compare model to observed frequencies.

7.SP.7a.description: Develop a uniform probability model (equal probability to all outcomes).

7.SP.7b.description: Develop a probability model by observing frequencies in data.

7.SP.8.cluster: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models
7.SP.8.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

7.SP.8a.description: Probability of compound event = fraction of outcomes in sample space for which event occurs.

7.SP.8b.description: Represent sample spaces using organized lists, tables, and tree diagrams.

7.SP.8c.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.

8.NS.1.cluster: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers
8.NS.1.description: Know that non-rational numbers are called irrational. Show rational numbers have repeating decimal expansions. Convert repeating decimals to fractions.

8.NS.2.cluster: Know that there are numbers that are not rational, and approximate them by rational numbers
8.NS.2.description: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare them and locate on number line.

8.EE.1.cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
8.EE.1.description: Know and apply properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent expressions.

8.EE.2.cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
8.EE.2.description: Use square root and cube root symbols. Evaluate square roots of perfect squares and cube roots of perfect cubes. Know √2 is irrational.

8.EE.3.cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
8.EE.3.description: Use numbers in the form single digit × integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities.

8.EE.4.cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
8.EE.4.description: Perform operations with numbers in scientific notation. Use scientific notation with appropriate units.

8.EE.5.cluster: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations
8.EE.5.description: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as slope. Compare two proportional relationships.

8.EE.6.cluster: Understand the connections between proportional relationships, lines, and linear equations
8.EE.6.description: Use similar triangles to explain why slope is constant. Derive y = mx and y = mx + b.

8.EE.7.cluster: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations
8.EE.7.description: Solve linear equations in one variable.

8.EE.7a.description: Give examples of linear equations with one solution, infinitely many, or no solutions.

8.EE.7b.description: Solve linear equations with rational coefficients, including distributive property and collecting like terms.

8.EE.8.cluster: Analyze and solve linear equations and pairs of simultaneous linear equations
8.EE.8.description: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

8.EE.8a.description: Solutions to a system correspond to points of intersection of their graphs.

8.EE.8b.description: Solve systems of two linear equations algebraically and by graphing. Solve simple cases by inspection.

8.EE.8c.description: Solve real-world problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.

8.F.1.description: Understand that a function assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph is the set of ordered pairs.

8.F.2.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented differently (algebraically, graphically, numerically, verbally).

8.F.3.description: Interpret y = mx + b as defining a linear function. Give examples of non-linear functions.

8.F.4.cluster: Use functions to model relationships between quantities
8.F.4.description: Construct a function to model a linear relationship. Determine rate of change and initial value from description, table, or graph.

8.F.5.cluster: Use functions to model relationships between quantities
8.F.5.description: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph. Sketch a graph from verbal description.

8.G.1.cluster: Understand congruence and similarity using physical models, transparencies, or geometry software
8.G.1.description: Verify experimentally properties of rotations, reflections, and translations (lines→lines, angles preserved, parallels preserved).

8.G.1a.description: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.

8.G.1b.description: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.

8.G.1c.description: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.

8.G.2.description: A 2D figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained by a sequence of rigid motions.

8.G.3.description: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on 2D figures using coordinates.

8.G.4.description: A 2D figure is similar to another if the second is obtained by rigid motions followed by a dilation.

8.G.5.description: Use informal arguments for angle sum of triangles, exterior angles, angles from parallel lines cut by transversal, and AA similarity.

8.G.6.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem
8.G.6.description: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.

8.G.7.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem
8.G.7.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in real-world and mathematical problems in 2D and 3D.

8.G.8.cluster: Understand and apply the Pythagorean Theorem
8.G.8.description: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.

8.G.9.cluster: Solve real-world problems involving volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres
8.G.9.description: Know the formulas for volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve problems.

8.SP.1.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data
8.SP.1.description: Construct and interpret scatter plots. Describe patterns: clustering, outliers, positive/negative/linear/nonlinear association.

8.SP.2.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data
8.SP.2.description: Know straight lines model relationships. Informally fit a line to scatter plot data suggesting linear association.

8.SP.3.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data
8.SP.3.description: Use equation of a linear model to solve problems in context. Interpret slope and intercept.

8.SP.4.cluster: Investigate patterns of association in bivariate data
8.SP.4.description: Understand patterns in bivariate categorical data via two-way tables. Construct and interpret two-way tables.

HSN-RN.1.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
HSN-RN.1.cluster: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents
HSN-RN.1.description: Explain how the definition of rational exponents follows from extending properties of integer exponents.

HSN-RN.2.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
HSN-RN.2.cluster: Extend the properties of exponents to rational exponents
HSN-RN.2.description: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using properties of exponents.

HSN-RN.3.domain: Number and Quantity — The Real Number System
HSN-RN.3.cluster: Use properties of rational and irrational numbers
HSN-RN.3.description: Explain why sum/product of rationals is rational; sum of rational+irrational is irrational; product of nonzero rational and irrational is irrational.

HSN-Q.1.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
HSN-Q.1.description: Use units to understand problems and guide multi-step solutions. Choose and interpret units and scales.

HSN-Q.2.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
HSN-Q.2.description: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.

HSN-Q.3.cluster: Reason quantitatively and use units to solve problems
HSN-Q.3.description: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.

HSN-CN.1.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
HSN-CN.1.cluster: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers
HSN-CN.1.description: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = –1. Every complex number has form a + bi.

HSN-CN.2.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
HSN-CN.2.cluster: Perform arithmetic operations with complex numbers
HSN-CN.2.description: Use i² = –1 and commutative, associative, distributive properties to add, subtract, multiply complex numbers.

HSN-CN.7.domain: Number and Quantity — The Complex Number System
HSN-CN.7.cluster: Use complex numbers in polynomial identities and equations
HSN-CN.7.description: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.

HSA-SSE.1.description: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of context. Interpret parts (terms, factors, coefficients).

HSA-SSE.1a.description: Interpret parts of an expression such as terms, factors, and coefficients.

HSA-SSE.1b.description: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more parts as a single entity.

HSA-SSE.2.description: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it (e.g., difference of squares).

HSA-SSE.3.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
HSA-SSE.3.description: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal properties of the quantity.

HSA-SSE.3a.description: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal zeros of the function it defines.

HSA-SSE.3b.description: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal maximum or minimum.

HSA-SSE.3c.description: Use properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.

HSA-SSE.4.cluster: Write expressions in equivalent forms to solve problems
HSA-SSE.4.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series and use it to solve problems.

HSA-APR.1.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
HSA-APR.1.description: Polynomials are closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication. Add, subtract, multiply polynomials.

HSA-APR.2.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
HSA-APR.2.cluster: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
HSA-APR.2.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem.

HSA-APR.3.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
HSA-APR.3.cluster: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials
HSA-APR.3.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available. Use zeros to construct rough graph.

HSA-APR.4.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
HSA-APR.4.cluster: Use polynomial identities to solve problems
HSA-APR.4.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.

HSA-APR.6.domain: Algebra — Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
HSA-APR.6.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x)/b(x) in form q(x) + r(x)/b(x).

HSA-CED.1.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
HSA-CED.1.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems (linear, quadratic, rational, exponential).

HSA-CED.2.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
HSA-CED.2.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships. Graph on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

HSA-CED.3.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
HSA-CED.3.description: Represent constraints by equations/inequalities and systems. Interpret solutions as viable or non-viable in context.

HSA-CED.4.cluster: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships
HSA-CED.4.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest.

HSA-REI.1.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.1.cluster: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning
HSA-REI.1.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

HSA-REI.2.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.2.cluster: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning
HSA-REI.2.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations. Give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

HSA-REI.3.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.3.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
HSA-REI.3.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including with coefficients represented by letters.

HSA-REI.4.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.4.cluster: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable
HSA-REI.4.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

HSA-REI.4a.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.4a.description: Complete the square to transform quadratic to (x – p)² = q. Derive the quadratic formula.

HSA-REI.4b.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.4b.description: Solve quadratics by inspection, square roots, completing the square, quadratic formula, and factoring. Recognize complex solutions.

HSA-REI.5.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.5.description: Prove that replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

HSA-REI.6.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.6.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs).

HSA-REI.7.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.7.description: Solve a system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation algebraically and graphically.

HSA-REI.10.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.10.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
HSA-REI.10.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane.

HSA-REI.11.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.11.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
HSA-REI.11.description: Explain why x-coordinates of intersection points of y = f(x) and y = g(x) are solutions of f(x) = g(x).

HSA-REI.12.domain: Algebra — Reasoning with Equations and Inequalities
HSA-REI.12.cluster: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically
HSA-REI.12.description: Graph solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane. Graph solution set of a system of linear inequalities.

HSF-IF.1.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
HSF-IF.1.description: Understand function from domain to range assigns each input exactly one output. f(x) notation. Graph of f is y = f(x).

HSF-IF.2.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
HSF-IF.2.description: Use function notation, evaluate functions, and interpret statements using function notation in context.

HSF-IF.3.cluster: Understand the concept of a function and use function notation
HSF-IF.3.description: Recognize that sequences are functions, sometimes defined recursively, whose domain is a subset of integers.

HSF-IF.4.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
HSF-IF.4.description: Interpret key features of graphs and tables (intercepts, increasing/decreasing, maxima/minima, symmetry, end behavior, periodicity).

HSF-IF.5.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
HSF-IF.5.description: Relate the domain of a function to its graph and to the quantitative relationship it describes.

HSF-IF.6.cluster: Interpret functions that arise in applications in terms of the context
HSF-IF.6.description: Calculate and interpret the average rate of change of a function over a specified interval.

HSF-IF.7.description: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph.

HSF-IF.7a.description: Graph linear and quadratic functions and show intercepts, maxima, and minima.

HSF-IF.7b.description: Graph square root, cube root, and piecewise-defined functions, including step and absolute value.

HSF-IF.7c.description: Graph polynomial functions, identifying zeros and showing end behavior.

HSF-IF.7e.description: Graph exponential and logarithmic functions showing intercepts and end behavior; graph trigonometric functions showing period, midline, amplitude.

HSF-IF.8.description: Write a function in different but equivalent forms to reveal and explain different properties.

HSF-IF.8a.description: Factor and complete the square in a quadratic to show zeros, extrema, and symmetry.

HSF-IF.8b.description: Use properties of exponents to interpret expressions for exponential functions (percent rate of change, growth/decay).

HSF-IF.9.description: Compare properties of two functions each represented differently.

HSF-BF.1.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
HSF-BF.1.description: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities.

HSF-BF.1a.description: Determine an explicit expression, recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.

HSF-BF.1b.description: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.

HSF-BF.2.cluster: Build a function that models a relationship between two quantities
HSF-BF.2.description: Write arithmetic and geometric sequences both recursively and explicitly. Model situations, translate between forms.

HSF-BF.3.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions
HSF-BF.3.description: Identify the effect on graph of f(x) + k, kf(x), f(kx), f(x + k). Recognize even and odd functions.

HSF-BF.4.cluster: Build new functions from existing functions

HSF-BF.4a.description: Solve f(x) = c for a simple function with an inverse. Write expression for the inverse.

HSF-LE.1.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.1.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
HSF-LE.1.description: Distinguish between situations modeled with linear vs. exponential functions.

HSF-LE.1a.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.1a.description: Prove linear functions grow by equal differences over equal intervals; exponentials grow by equal factors.

HSF-LE.1b.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.1b.description: Recognize situations with constant rate of change per unit interval.

HSF-LE.1c.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.1c.description: Recognize situations with constant percent rate of change per unit interval.

HSF-LE.2.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.2.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
HSF-LE.2.description: Construct linear and exponential functions (including arithmetic and geometric sequences) given graph, description, or input-output pairs.

HSF-LE.3.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.3.cluster: Construct and compare linear, quadratic, and exponential models and solve problems
HSF-LE.3.description: Observe that a quantity increasing exponentially eventually exceeds one increasing linearly or polynomially.

HSF-LE.5.domain: Functions — Linear, Quadratic, and Exponential Models
HSF-LE.5.cluster: Interpret expressions for functions in terms of the situation they model
HSF-LE.5.description: Interpret the parameters in a linear or exponential function in terms of a context.

HSF-TF.1.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
HSF-TF.1.description: Understand radian measure as the length of the arc on the unit circle subtended by the angle.

HSF-TF.2.cluster: Extend the domain of trigonometric functions using the unit circle
HSF-TF.2.description: Explain how the unit circle extends trigonometric functions to all real numbers.

HSF-TF.5.cluster: Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions
HSF-TF.5.description: Choose trigonometric functions to model periodic phenomena with specified amplitude, frequency, and midline.

HSF-TF.8.description: Prove the Pythagorean identity sin²(θ) + cos²(θ) = 1 and use it to find trig values given one value and quadrant.

HSG-CO.1.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
HSG-CO.1.description: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment.

HSG-CO.2.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
HSG-CO.2.description: Represent transformations as functions that take points as inputs and give other points as outputs.

HSG-CO.3.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
HSG-CO.3.description: Describe rotations and reflections that carry a rectangle, parallelogram, trapezoid, or regular polygon onto itself.

HSG-CO.4.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
HSG-CO.4.description: Develop definitions of rotations, reflections, and translations in terms of angles, circles, perpendicular/parallel lines.

HSG-CO.5.cluster: Experiment with transformations in the plane
HSG-CO.5.description: Given a figure and transformation, draw the transformed figure. Specify a sequence of transformations mapping one figure to another.

HSG-CO.6.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
HSG-CO.6.description: Use rigid motions to transform figures and predict effects. Use definition of congruence via rigid motions.

HSG-CO.7.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
HSG-CO.7.description: Two triangles are congruent iff corresponding sides and angles are congruent (via rigid motions).

HSG-CO.8.cluster: Understand congruence in terms of rigid motions
HSG-CO.8.description: Explain how triangle congruence criteria (ASA, SAS, SSS) follow from rigid motions.

HSG-CO.9.description: Prove theorems about lines and angles (vertical angles, transversals with parallel lines, perpendicular bisectors).

HSG-CO.10.description: Prove theorems about triangles (angle sum 180°, base angles of isosceles, midsegment, medians meet at a point).

HSG-CO.11.description: Prove theorems about parallelograms (opposite sides/angles congruent, diagonals bisect, rectangles have congruent diagonals).

HSG-CO.12.description: Make formal geometric constructions with various tools (copy segment/angle, bisect, construct perpendicular/parallel lines).

HSG-CO.13.description: Construct an equilateral triangle, a square, and a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle.

HSG-SRT.1.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.1.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
HSG-SRT.1.description: Verify experimentally properties of dilations given by center and scale factor.

HSG-SRT.2.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.2.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
HSG-SRT.2.description: Use definition of similarity via similarity transformations. Explain similarity for triangles (equal angles, proportional sides).

HSG-SRT.3.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.3.cluster: Understand similarity in terms of similarity transformations
HSG-SRT.3.description: Use properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA criterion for similarity.

HSG-SRT.4.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.4.description: Prove theorems about triangles (line parallel to one side divides other two proportionally; Pythagorean Theorem via similarity).

HSG-SRT.5.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.5.description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems and prove relationships.

HSG-SRT.6.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.6.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
HSG-SRT.6.description: By similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles, leading to definitions of trigonometric ratios.

HSG-SRT.7.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.7.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
HSG-SRT.7.description: Explain and use the relationship between sine and cosine of complementary angles.

HSG-SRT.8.domain: Geometry — Similarity, Right Triangles, and Trigonometry
HSG-SRT.8.cluster: Define trigonometric ratios and solve problems involving right triangles
HSG-SRT.8.description: Use trigonometric ratios and Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

HSG-C.1.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
HSG-C.1.description: Prove that all circles are similar.

HSG-C.2.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
HSG-C.2.description: Identify and describe relationships among inscribed angles, radii, and chords.

HSG-C.3.cluster: Understand and apply theorems about circles
HSG-C.3.description: Construct inscribed and circumscribed circles of a triangle. Prove properties of angles for inscribed quadrilateral.

HSG-C.5.cluster: Find arc lengths and areas of sectors of circles
HSG-C.5.description: Derive using similarity that arc length is proportional to radius. Define radian measure. Derive area of a sector.

HSG-GPE.1.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.1.cluster: Translate between geometric description and equation for a conic section
HSG-GPE.1.description: Derive equation of a circle using Pythagorean Theorem. Complete the square to find center and radius.

HSG-GPE.2.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.2.cluster: Translate between geometric description and equation for a conic section
HSG-GPE.2.description: Derive the equation of a parabola given a focus and directrix.

HSG-GPE.4.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.4.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
HSG-GPE.4.description: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically.

HSG-GPE.5.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.5.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
HSG-GPE.5.description: Prove slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines. Use them to solve problems.

HSG-GPE.6.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.6.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
HSG-GPE.6.description: Find the point on a directed line segment that partitions it in a given ratio.

HSG-GPE.7.domain: Geometry — Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
HSG-GPE.7.cluster: Use coordinates to prove simple geometric theorems algebraically
HSG-GPE.7.description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles.

HSG-GMD.1.cluster: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
HSG-GMD.1.description: Give informal argument for formulas for circumference, area of circle, volume of cylinder, pyramid, cone.

HSG-GMD.3.cluster: Explain volume formulas and use them to solve problems
HSG-GMD.3.description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems.

HSG-GMD.4.description: Identify shapes of 2D cross-sections of 3D objects, and 3D objects generated by rotations of 2D objects.

HSG-MG.1.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
HSG-MG.1.description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and properties to describe objects (e.g., model a tree trunk as a cylinder).

HSG-MG.2.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
HSG-MG.2.description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume in modeling situations.

HSG-MG.3.cluster: Apply geometric concepts in modeling situations
HSG-MG.3.description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems (physical constraints, minimize cost, typographic grids).

HSS-ID.1.domain: Statistics and Probability — Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data
HSS-ID.1.cluster: Summarize, represent, and interpret data on a single count or measurement variable
HSS-ID.1.description: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, box plots).

HSS-ID.2.domain: Statistics and Probability — Interpreting Categorical and Quantitative Data
